beats.care: Cheap Wi-Fi cameras are in many Indian homes and PGs. Change the default password, update the app, and don't point cameras at sensitive spots.
beats.what: A Wall Street Journal investigation found spies and hackers taking over internet cameras, from traffic cams to home webcams, to watch troops and targets.
beats.why: In 2024, Russian hackers reportedly used home webcams in Kyiv to aim missile strikes. Dutch intelligence says Russia hacks European cameras to track arms.

cards.body: Hackers backing Ukraine took over a camera in Sevastopol in 2022 and tracked a Russian helicopter to an unknown air base, which was then struck. In Israel, a farmer found his camera was being used to watch troops near the Lebanon border.
Its security service says Russia could have used them to spot targets and correct strikes.
cards.caption: Risky cameras Ukraine has blocked or moved since 2022

cards.body: An Iran-linked hacker group taunted Israelis to 'find the nearest traffic camera and talk'.

cards.q: Would you keep a camera inside your home?

opts: Hacked feeds let spies watch troops and targets
cards.q: Why are ordinary cameras useful in a war?
cards.why: Millions of poorly protected cameras become free spy eyes once someone breaks in.

hook: Could your *home CCTV* end up spying for someone else?

learn.t: There are about 1.2 billion internet-connected cameras worldwide, in doorbells, traffic lights and baby monitors, and many have little protection.
